title: PAULA - Perspectives on Support, Living Environments, and Childhood Obesity
summary:
Background
Obesity in childhood and adolescence can affect the physical and mental health as well as the daily lives of the children and adolescents affected and their families. Treatment often encompasses various areas, such as nutrition, physical activity, medical care, and psychosocial support. However, it can be difficult for families to find appropriate programs, participate in them regularly, and implement recommendations in their daily lives over the long term. Long commutes, a lack of available services, time constraints, or experiences with exclusion and weight stigma can also play a role.
To date, there is insufficient knowledge about how children and adolescents with obesity, as well as their parents, experience the existing care system, which services they use, and in which areas they would like more support.

Research Question
The PAULA study examines how children and adolescents with obesity, as well as their parents, experience care and support. In particular, the study focuses on the following areas:

- Treatment and support services used to date
- Experiences with care received to date
- Difficulties and barriers to participating in services and implementing them in daily life
- Wishes and additional support needs

The goal is to identify strengths and potential gaps in care. The results are intended to help better tailor future support services to the needs of children, adolescents, and their families.

Method
The study is being conducted as an online survey at several medical centers in Germany. Children and adolescents with obesity, as well as their parents or caregivers, are eligible to participate. The survey is conducted online. Children, adolescents, and parents each receive their own questionnaire, tailored to their respective perspectives.

interventions.name: Parents of children and adolescents with obesity

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Children and Adolescents
•Children and adolescents (ages 10–21) with obesity (age- and gender-specific BMI above the 97th percentile) or severe obesity (age- and gender-specific BMI above the 99.5th percentile)
•Sufficient language proficiency to complete the questionnaire
•Stable internet access

Parents
•Parents or legal guardians of a child (ages 0–21) with obesity (age- and gender-specific BMI above the 97th percentile) or severe obesity (age- and gender-specific BMI above the 99.5th percentile)
•Sufficient language proficiency to complete the questionnaire
•Stable internet access
Exclusion criteria:
None
